archetype: Golgari -1/-1-counter aristocrats: place counters, turn each placement into a body, turn bodies into drain, and hold three Mikaeus kill lines on top. strategic_frame.json declares `combo` and deck-audit adopts it, applying combo's overrides. The frame agrees with the deck: 8 tutors against combo's 4-8 and 5 protection against 4-6 both land inside the override bands.
verdict: This deck functions and it converts. It casts a 2-mana commander on turn 2 in 9,970 of 10,000 goldfish games, hits the turn-3 land drop 90.2% of the time with zero unconditional taplands, and assembles commander-plus-a-payoff 67.2% of the time. What limits it is that every answer it owns points at a creature: across all 88 entries in cards.json, exactly two cards destroy anything (Crumbling Ashes, Mikaeus) and both destroy creatures, and nothing in the 99 destroys or exiles an artifact, an enchantment, or a land on the battlefield. One axis that reads as a problem is not: card-advantage's 8 misses The One Ring, Yawgmoth and Grim Backwoods. Ramp's 16 against 10-12 is a real overage of four copies. The one prescribed swap takes a single slot from it, Arcane Signet; a second ranked cut candidate, Dark Ritual, sits on the same axis and is not prescribed.

open_questions.question: Does Ivy Lane Denizen loop in this deck, and does it convert? It is in the 99 and appears in seven of the nineteen two-card entries bracket_report.json lists: with Scurry Oak, and with six of the eight mana-free sacrifice outlets (Ashnod's Altar, Phyrexian Altar, Carrion Feeder, Viscera Seer, Yahenni, Blasting Station).
open_questions.why_it_matters: Ivy Lane Denizen is the load-bearing unverified card, not Scurry Oak. Those seven entries are exactly the seven of nineteen that route through none of Mikaeus, Blowfly Infestation or the commander, so a ruling on the Denizen settles this deck's only cluster of kills that survives Mikaeus being answered — and six of the seven pair it with a class that is eight deep, which would make the line redundant rather than a single point of failure. Mikaeus appears in 8 entries and Ivy Lane Denizen in 7; nothing else appears in more than 3. It is also one scenario rather than seven, since the six outlet records differ only in which free outlet is on the board. Note for whoever writes it: Ivy Lane Denizen triggers only when another green creature you control enters, and none of those six records names a card that puts a creature onto the battlefield repeatedly — that gap is the thing to resolve.

open_questions.question: Is Hapatra + Blowfly Infestation actually a two-card kill? goldfish_targets.json declares it as one and the audit measures it at 16.3% assembled (66.7% with tutors), but no stack has ever resolved it.
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the deck's second-most-measured target and its declared kill with the commander. Every number reported for it is a number about drawing two cards, not about winning.

open_questions.question: What is this deck's real rate of assembling ANY kill, rather than each named one separately?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The audit says outright that the schema cannot express the union of independent kills, and goldfish_targets.json declares no target at all for either non-Mikaeus route. So the simulator has never measured the deck's most redundant path to a win, and 2.5% and 16.3% both understate it by an unknown amount.

open_questions.question: Do the three Blowfly Infestation entries and the Hapatra + Host of the Hereafter entry survive a resolve-stack run, and what is the defensible two-card-infinite count?
open_questions.why_it_matters: bracket_report.json lists 19: 8 Mikaeus, 7 Ivy Lane Denizen, 3 Blowfly Infestation and Hapatra + Host of the Hereafter. Stack 001 refuted six of the eight Mikaeus entries and calls the figure inflated; open_questions[0] takes the seven Denizen entries. That leaves the three Blowfly entries (Nest of Scarabs, Flourishing Defenses, Hapatra) and the Host of the Hereafter entry, which nothing in the repo has ever examined. The floor of 4 does not depend on any of it — the 11 Game Changers force 4 by themselves — but a combo count nobody can defend is how a prescription gets sized against a number that is not there.

gaps: No deck_recon.json exists for this deck (deck-audit freshness reports recon absent), so nothing here is weighed against what strong Hapatra lists actually run. The single prescribed add comes from the deck's own colour-identity pool. A deck-recon pass would settle whether the format's answer to this hole is Assassin's Trophy or something the pool never surfaced.

bracket_report.json carries no decklist_sha256, so deck-audit cannot show it current. Its combo_count of 32 and its Mikaeus + Ashnod's Altar example are both contradicted by stack 001; treat the floor of 4 as resting on the Game Changer list alone.

Abstergo Entertainment exiles all graveyards, but it carries only land:fixing / land:untapped-dual / land:utility roles, and the breadth function reads oracle text only on cards holding an interactive role. The measured 1 therefore understates real coverage by one class — the deck's true position is 2 of 5, not 1 of 5, and the artifact, enchantment and land classes are genuinely empty. This is also why the prescription is one card and not two: Assassin's Trophy closes all three genuinely empty classes by itself, so after it the deck answers every class in Magic terms while the measure still reads 4.

Talon Gates of Madara phases out a creature on entry and Svogthos, the Restless Tomb is the one card in the 99 with no card_roles entry at all (roles coverage 98.9%). Neither changes a count here, but both are invisible to every role-driven axis.

Whether the interaction-breadth floor of 5 is the right target for a combo deck that wins from a board of dying creatures is a judgement the corpus does not make per-archetype; the target is the same one it sets for every deck.

The cut list now carries no `painful` entry. Necroskitter was it, and the entry is dropped rather than re-rated, because its premise was inverted. Of the eleven cards in the 99 that place a -1/-1 counter — the enumeration in engine.single_points_of_failure[1] — only Devoted Druid is confined to a creature you control, and it counters itself as a mana cost. The other ten can each put one on a creature an opponent controls, and every one of them except Necroskitter itself is on deck-audit's 14-card interaction axis: the counter suite and the removal suite are the same cards. Crumbling Ashes reads "At the beginning of your upkeep, destroy target creature with a -1/-1 counter on it", and Black Sun's Zenith puts X counters on each creature. So the deck's removal is what turns Necroskitter's reanimation trigger on, not what starves it. What survived the correction — three mana, 1 power, nothing against an empty opposing board — does not carry a cut on its own, and its wither fires on blocking as well as on attacking. Whether this deck has a genuinely painful cut is therefore unsettled. Ramp is the only axis deck-audit reads `over`, and cut_candidates[0] and [1] already take two copies of that surplus from the eight pure-mana pieces; the remaining six — Chrome Mox, Grim Monolith, Lotus Petal, Mana Vault, Mox Diamond, Sol Ring — are where a scoped pass would look.

findings.note: Scope holds exactly. I diffed the working diagnosis.json against `git show HEAD:data/decks/hapatra/diagnosis.json` leaf-by-leaf (flattened JSON paths). Removed: cut_candidates[3]'s six leaves (card, why, cost_of_cutting, difficulty, citations[0].rule, citations[0].quote; orphans_stack was [] and carries no leaf). Added: gaps[5]. CHANGED set is EMPTY — zero leaves altered anywhere else, so cut_candidates[0..2], all 16 axes, engine, lean_into, add_candidates, open_questions and gaps[0..4] are byte-identical to the document I reviewed at iteration 3. The prior `skeptic` block is also gone, which is the normal merge flow (the orchestrator re-merges this file); validate-diagnosis passes without it. No unannounced eighth leaf.

Removal, not re-rating, is the right call: I checked whether a real candidate was deleted for a merely-wrong argument, and the corrected facts destroy the substance of the cut, not just its wording. (a) Re-derived from cards.json myself: 14 of 88 entries contain the string '-1/-1 counter'; 11 of them PLACE one; the three that mention without placing are Crumbling Ashes (destroys), Flourishing Defenses and Nest of Scarabs (payoffs). (b) Reading all 11 oracle texts, only Devoted Druid ('Put a -1/-1 counter on this creature: Untap this creature') is confined to a creature you control — Hapatra, Black Sun's Zenith, Blowfly Infestation, Contagion Clasp, Fume Spitter, Grim Affliction, Necroskitter, Obelisk Spider, Serrated Arrows and Yawgmoth can each land one on an opponent's creature. (c) Against a fresh `deck-audit hapatra --out <dir>/`, the interaction axis (value 14) lists Black Sun's Zenith, Blasting Station, Blowfly Infestation, Contagion Clasp, Crumbling Ashes, Devoted Druid, Fume Spitter, Grim Affliction, Hapatra, Obelisk Spider, Orcish Bowmasters, Serrated Arrows, Walking Ballista, Yawgmoth — i.e. 10 of the 11 placers, all but Necroskitter itself. So the deck's removal suite IS its counter suite, and Crumbling Ashes ('At the beginning of your upkeep, destroy target creature with a -1/-1 counter on it') plus Black Sun's Zenith ('Put X -1/-1 counters on each creature') manufacture exactly the event Necroskitter's reanimation trigger is paid on. (d) Nothing else carries the cut: Necroskitter is on no axis the audit reads over — cutting it moves ramp 16, interaction 14, interaction-breadth 1 and threat-density 6 by zero, and only the informational creature count 25 to 24. A cut candidate whose argument is inverted AND whose removal moves no measured axis is correctly deleted rather than re-rated.

The eleven-placer enumeration this component rests on is exactly reproducible. My independent scan of cards.json returns the same eleven names in the same set (Hapatra, Black Sun's Zenith, Blowfly Infestation, Contagion Clasp, Devoted Druid, Fume Spitter, Grim Affliction, Necroskitter, Obelisk Spider, Serrated Arrows, Yawgmoth), and Host of the Hereafter is correctly filed as a twelfth outside the set — its text is 'put its counters on up to one target creature you control', which does not contain the '-1/-1 counter' string and only moves counters onto your own board. Toxic Deluge's exclusion is right ('All creatures get -X/-X until end of turn' — not counters). The gating claims still hold on the oracle text: Serrated Arrows is capped at three arrowhead counters, one per turn; Contagion Clasp places one on entry then proliferates for {4}; Black Sun's Zenith, Fume Spitter and Grim Affliction are one-shot; Yawgmoth is the only free, at-will, uncapped, any-target placer.

The 'wither fires on blocking' correction is TRUE and it does weaken the deleted entry's case. CR 120.3d, fetched via `lookup-rule 120.3d`: 'Damage dealt to a creature by a source with wither and/or infect causes that source's controller to put that many -1/-1 counters on that creature.' Nothing restricts it to attacking, so a 1/4 Necroskitter blocking places a counter — which is precisely the limb the deleted `why` leaned on ('its wither only fires on its own combat damage — a 1-power body attacking into a bracket-4 table'). The follow-on claim is also right and is the load-bearing half: because 120.3d says the SOURCE'S CONTROLLER puts the counters, wither damage satisfies the 'whenever YOU put one or more -1/-1 counters on a creature' trigger on Hapatra, Nest of Scarabs and Obelisk Spider, and Flourishing Defenses ('whenever a -1/-1 counter is put on a creature') needs no controller clause at all. I verified those four payoff texts in cards.json and confirmed they are the only four in the 99 that trigger on counter PLACEMENT — Crumbling Ashes and Necroskitter care about counters but trigger on death. One imprecision, noted rather than charged: Devoted Druid's counter is the cost of its untap ability, not literally 'a mana cost'; the substantive claim (self-confined) is correct.

The ramp arithmetic in the closing sentence is accurate.
